name: Bandinello Sauli
summary:
**Identity & Significance**: Bandinello Sauli (bandinello-sauli) was a prominent Italian Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal, appointed by Pope Julius III in 1550. This position marked the beginning of his career, which would span over three decades and take him to various regions across Europe.

**What Happened**: During his tenure as bishop, Sauli played a significant role in several diplomatic missions, including one to the Holy Roman Emperor Charles V in 1564. He also contributed to the Catholic Church's efforts to reform its liturgical practices, particularly through his involvement with the Council of Trent (1545-1563).

**Legacy & Consequence**: Sauli's work on the Council of Trent helped shape the modern liturgy of the Roman Catholic Church. His diplomatic missions further solidified the Church's influence in European politics.

**A Lasting Cultural Footprint**: Bandinello Sauli's legacy can be seen in the numerous churches and buildings he helped construct or renovate throughout Italy, including his namesake church in Rome, which still stands today.
